title: Seller Sparkplug: Technical Brief & Quickdeck (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, technical-first sales brief (deck sketch + speaker notes) intended for SEs and platform sellers who need a 5–8 minute engineering pitch for Redwood Inference. 

Context / why 'Sparkplug':
- Quick, energetic framing to get an engineer engaged in the first 60s.
- Emphasizes predictable latency, cost levers, and safe fallbacks (the things platform teams actually measure).
- Designed to transition straight into a pilot checklist or technical PoC.

Structure (what SE should cover in order):
1) 30s hook: "We help you make inference predictable — under your SLA and budget."
   - Two quick numbers: median 95th percentile latency under X tokens (replace with product benchmark during prep).
2) Top causes of surprise in inference (ops pain): cold KV-cache misses, burst patterns, model fallbacks, noisy prompts.
3) How Redwood addresses each: kernel selection, smart routing, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles, canary rollouts.
4) Pilot proposal: 2-week narrow-scope pilot; measurable SLOs and rollback plan.
5) Quick FAQ + escalation path.

One-slide script (SE speaker notes):
- Slide title: "Predictable Inference, Not Just Fast"
- Bullet script: "Most teams see spikes in token cost when their workload has unseen contexts; we mitigate that with auto prefix cache + routing to a cheaper quantized variant if latency budget is hit. Example: customer X cut per-token spend by ~28% on chat history workloads after enabling cache."
- Call to action: "Can we run a 2-week pilot on a single route? We'll attach SLOs and a rollback trigger."

Pilot checklist (minimal viable pilot):
- Scope: 1 service route or 1 API key, stable traffic (>= 10 req/s) for at least 48h during test windows.
- Baseline capture: collect token distribution, sequence-length histogram, 95th pct latency for 48h (SE help: use /metrics export or the trial dashboard).
- Config to test: enable prefix caching (30k tokens TTL), try batching policy A (max latency 120ms target), compare model variant (full fp16 vs 4-bit quant).
- SLOs: 95th pct latency <= target_ms; error rate < 0.5%; cost delta per 10k tokens (compare).
- Rollback: automatic fallback to hosted default if latency > SLA for 10m window.

Fallback matrix (talking points):
- Latency breach -> route to lower-capacity quantized model variant + notify via webhook.
- Capacity shortage/region outage -> cross-region routing to secondary pool (observable in Console).
- Quality regression -> auto-roll back to previous model version and trigger evaluation test set to measure drift.

SE objection playbook (short snippets):
- "We need on-prem only" -> "We support Redwood Private (VPC & on-prem). We can ship a hardened installer and integrate with customer KMS; recommend dedicated capacity pilot next."
- "Token costs are unpredictable" -> "We instrument per-route token breakdown and suggest batching + prefix caching; we can show projected unit economics before commit."
- "Latency targets are strict" -> "We offer Dedicated with SLA-backed latency tiers and can design a canary with traffic shaping to validate."

Quick technical appendix (for appendix slide or follow-up):
- Kernel selection: runtime picks kernels by matrix multiply profile; expect ~10–25% perf delta when switching kernels for attention patterns.
- KV cache warmup: recommend synthetic prewarm for long-context chat demos (tool: scripts/prewarm.sh in PR linked above).
- Quantization guidance: 4-bit works well for many instruction models, but run evaluation on customer prompts (we automate with Redwood Optimize).

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Replace placeholder benchmark numbers with the latest microbenchmarks (ask bench infra team; chat #benchmarks).
- Add a 1-slide visual showing routing fallback timeline (timeline graphic).
- Collect 2 anonymized mini-case stats for cost reduction and latency improvement to use as proof points.

Suggested assets to attach to the deck:
- One-page pilot SOW template (internal template link)
- Live console demo checklist (login instructions + demo script)
- Short gif of fallback routing flow (ops team to produce)

Speaker tips: keep it technical, call out trade-offs quickly (latency vs batch size vs model variant), and always end with a concrete next step (pilot scope, SLOs).

Annotated callout: sample rapid-qualify question set for the first discovery call:
- "What is your typical request size (avg tokens) and distribution?"
- "Do you require region residency or KMS control?"
- "What latency SLOs do you commit to your product users?"

Links / references (placeholders to fill):
- Confluence pilot page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sparkplug+Pilot+Notes

Version history notes (for reviewers):

- v0.2 (2025-11-10) added fallback matrix + pilot checklist (this file)

----

End of brief.
